dispositions.method: The automatic families of 1807 that reach 4 or more papers, long-running ones included (story_items.py --long-running), were split into single printed items (items.json: 177 items in 7 or more papers, 31 in 9 or more). Those items were read and the stories chosen by the rule below. Each chosen item's printings were looked for with phrase searches over all 4,167 pages of 1807 in both transcriptions (phrase_patterns.json, phrase_hits.json), and every hit was read. Papers with pages in a story's weeks but no printing were searched by hand with loose keywords. Every admitted printing was then checked against its page scan (SCAN_PROTOCOL.md, scan_points.json); 39 crops were placed by hand where the text-layer locator missed the passage.
dispositions.selection_rule: As for 1776: every single item printed in 9 or more newspapers was admitted, except digests of unrelated paragraphs and items that need careful framing. Items in 7 or 8 papers were chosen to cover the months and the main kinds of news. Stories are counted item by item; where one publication holds several documents (the Norfolk letters of July, the Chesapeake papers, the Burr affair), each document is its own group under a parent story. Every group reaches 7 or more papers. A paper that printed an item again later counts each printing.
added_by_phrase_search: BJ 1807-04-24 p2: a summary of Marshall's opinion of 1 April in a Richmond report (condensed report), found by the hand search
WR 1807-07-30 p2: a shorter, third-person account of Tazewell's report (condensed report)
LS 1807-09-10 p3: the verdict in the account most papers printed, on a torn page whose transcription keeps only fragments, found by the hand search

counted_item_by_item.Laws printed by authority: The acts repealing the salt duties, continuing the suspension of trade with parts of St. Domingo, on Virginia military warrants and prohibiting the importation of slaves were each counted in 9 or 10 papers because their titles also stand in the List of Acts and in reports of debates; by their enacting text they reach 3 to 7 papers.
counted_item_by_item.The President's message of 22 January: The message and its enclosures (Wilkinson's affidavit, letters of Burr and Bollman) are one publication, counted once by the message's opening.
counted_item_by_item.The Norfolk letters of July: Four documents printed together (Douglas's letter, the Mayor's answer, Tazewell's report, Douglas's second letter), each its own group under a parent story.
counted_item_by_item.The Burr verdict: Quoted in three different accounts of the court's proceedings; the group is the verdict as quoted (quoted_document).

not_admitted.The List of Acts passed during the secon: An index of unrelated laws, treated like a digest.
not_admitted.Other laws printed by authority: By their enacting text in fewer than 9 papers: the salt duties (5), Virginia military warrants (7; a weekly legal notice in the Virginia Argus), the suspension of the non-importation act (1). The proclamation suspending that act further (7 papers) was not chosen.
not_admitted.News digests: Runs of London and continental paragraphs printed in pieces (the London news by the Manchester packet, the Hamburg and Berlin paragraphs of January). Single paragraphs that reach 9 papers are admitted (Harford Jones).
not_admitted.Other Burr items: The President's messages of 28 January and 10 February (3 papers or fewer by their openings); reports that Burr was bailed at Natchez (4); a Richmond report of his examination that misstates the outcome (PGz, NHG, April); a NHG commentary of 6 October quoting the verdict.
not_admitted.The President's message of 19 February w: Counted under Monroe and Pinkney's letter where the letter is printed, not otherwise.
not_admitted.The court of inquiry's opening days (5 p: A different item from the court's opinion.
not_admitted.Candidates in 7 or 8 papers not chosen i: The House committee's second report on aggressions (8); the proclamation pardoning army deserters (7); the War Department's circular on volunteer companies (7); the Norfolk and Portsmouth resolutions of 24 June (7); a London report of peace between England, Russia and Turkey (7); the articles of the peace of Tilsit (7); the report that Britain disclaims searching ships of war (7); Bennigsen's dispatch of 10 February (7).
not_admitted.The Embargo: The President's message of 18 December (4 papers) and the Embargo Act of 22 December (5 papers by 31 December); most printings fall in January 1808.

for_user_decision.The act to prohibit the importation of s: Printed in full by authority in NI, a VA extra, HUS, NHG and an EN extra; its title in the List of Acts (10 papers) and in House debates on amending it.
for_user_decision.News from the Republic of Hayti (Baltimo: Christophe's attack on Port-au-Prince and a republican constitution; ADA also printed the constitution. The act on trade with parts of St. Domingo is in 3 papers.
for_user_decision.Robert MacDonald's death and funeral (No: A named seaman wounded on the Chesapeake; Fourth of July toasts in two papers name the men who died.
for_user_decision.The National Intelligencer on the seamen: Names the four men taken from the Chesapeake and describes their birthplaces and looks.
for_user_decision.General Wilkinson's speech in the court: About his arrest of Dr. Bollman, held without trial.
for_user_decision.Names in admitted stories, outside the e: The Burr documents name people arrested on suspicion; the House committee's report names the seamen; two Charleston reports name John Pierce, killed by a shot from the Leander. The excerpts end before these names.
